definition: Test items appearing in training data and inflating benchmark scores, and across 12 sources a problem the archive treats as mostly unmeasurable in the field. Four findings shape that view. Detection is fragile to the training pipeline: contamination introduced at the supervised stage is identifiable, and a brief reinforcement-learning run markedly suppresses the signals detectors rely on -- attributed to importance sampling and clipping rather than to any specific algorithm, so a broad class of post-training launders what preceded it. A negative audit is ambiguous: a detector returning no evidence has said either that the benchmark is clean or that the audit had too little power, and nothing in the literature separates them. Exposure mechanism matters: verbatim, paraphrase and surface-shuffle exposure produce sharply different behavioural signals, so a result established under one does not cover the others, and simulated contamination by mixing test items into a fine-tuning corpus produces verbatim-style exposure specifically. And mitigation metrics can be gamed by damage: one aggregate scores a synthetic strategy that makes the contaminated model fail every question better than no intervention at all, because over-suppression cancels against residual contamination -- a stratified reading ranks the same strategy worst. The practical instruments the corpus offers are a leakage ladder (question-only, empty, random, shuffled, matched, full-solution answer-recovery rates) and similarity audits reported with their false positives inspected by hand; both establish implausibility rather than absence.

evidence.note: Shows that the standard metric for judging contamination-mitigation strategies can be scored by cancellation rather than by restoration, replaces it with a per-question stratified metric under which the published ranking reverses, and proposes a mitigation that decides its intervention during decoding instead of from a prior estimate.
evidence.title: Zero Gap Is Not Restoration: Stratified Per-Question Probability Evaluation and Step-wise Mitigation of Benchmark Contamination

evidence.note: Casts benchmark contamination auditing as sparse-mixture detection, proves that detectability is governed by the single quantity alpha*rho*sqrt(m), and shows empirically that the resulting power predictions transport while the sample-size budgets derived from them do not.
evidence.title: When Is Benchmark Contamination Detectable? Information Limits and Power-Calibrated Audits

evidence.note: Compares chain-of-thought against answer-only supervision under a protocol where the two conditions differ in nothing but the training target, and finds the rationales buy nothing in-domain for strong backbones while buying 20 to 28 points out of domain -- with a human study attributing the measurable effect to language adherence and inspectability rather than to better reasoning.
evidence.title: MathShikkha: A Controlled Study of Answer-Only and Chain-of-Thought Supervision for Bangla Mathematical Reasoning in Small Language Models

evidence.note: Builds an industrial-safety reasoning benchmark from two pipelines -- program execution over safety scene graphs, and evidence graphs extracted from real accident-investigation reports -- and shows that general multimodal capability does not transfer to it while a 9B model fine-tuned on its chain-of-thought split matches frontier systems.
evidence.title: SafeSceneReason: A Multimodal Reasoning Benchmark Connecting Industrial Hazards with Accident Knowledge

evidence.note: Gives the teacher branch of an on-policy self-distillation setup an abstract skill card -- a principle, when it applies, and the mistakes to avoid -- instead of the reference solution, so the privileged signal carries no answer and the gain lands on exactly the rollout groups where group-relative reward is algebraically silent.
evidence.title: Distill Skills into Weights, Not Prompts: Abstract Skills as Privileged Signals for On-Policy Self-Distillation

evidence.note: Calibrates feature-based data-contamination detectors against the systematic feature shifts that post-training introduces, by measuring how controlled prompt variants move scores on known non-members and then correcting only the recurring shift directions, with the gains concentrated at the low-false-positive operating point rather than in AUC.
evidence.title: Calibrating Post-Training Feature Shifts for LLM Data Contamination Detection

evidence.note: A financial reasoning benchmark built from parameterized symbolic templates with executable Python, giving machine-verifiable step-level ground truth and contamination-free regeneration.
evidence.title: FinChain: A Symbolic Benchmark for Verifiable Chain-of-Thought Financial Reasoning

evidence.note: A business-domain benchmark pairing four knowledge areas with three practitioner roles, designed to trace application performance back to the theoretical capability it depends on.
evidence.title: BizCompass: Benchmarking the Reasoning Capabilities of LLMs in Business Knowledge and Applications

evidence.note: An inductive-reasoning benchmark from historical linguistics that requires inducing cascades of string-rewrite programs, with automated contamination-resistant generation and controllable difficulty.
evidence.title: PBEBench: A Multi-Step Programming by Examples Reasoning Benchmark inspired by Historical Linguistics

evidence.note: Shows that benchmark contamination in reasoning models is alarmingly easy to hide: a brief round of GRPO erases the signals contamination detectors rely on, and PPO-style importance sampling and clipping are identified as the cause — implying a broad class of RL methods conceals contamination inherently.
evidence.title: On The Fragility of Benchmark Contamination Detection in Reasoning Models

evidence.note: Converts AMC23 and AIME24/25 into symbolic templates whose constants are replaced by sampled variables, requires a model to solve several instantiations of each problem, and finds RL-finetuned models lose most of their reported accuracy under that consistency requirement.
evidence.title: VAR-MATH: Probing True Mathematical Reasoning in LLMs via Symbolic Multi-Instance Benchmarks

evidence.note: Shows that base models win pass@K on mathematics by producing wrong chains that land on right answers, and that scoring the chain too — CoT-Pass@K — reverses the verdict in RLVR's favour at every K.
evidence.title: Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards Implicitly Incentivizes Correct Reasoning in Base LLMs

name: benchmark contamination
